title: Finite stalk modules are retracts of global module stalks
statement: Let C be a category essentially small in the coefficient universe, J a Grothendieck topology, R a sheaf of commutative rings, p a point of Sh(C,J), and s a normalized ringed-site point [def-sfb-ringed-site-point], with stalk ring A and module functor S. For each finitely presented A-module M [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], there exists a sheaf F of R-modules such that M is a retract of S(F). No finite-limit or subcanonical hypothesis on the site is needed.

source.place: Tag 0DEN, finite-presentation test step; universal finite matrix construction replaces local descent

proof.text: Write M as the cokernel of a finite matrix f:A^ι→A^κ. Let T be the finite product of copies of the underlying set sheaf of R indexed by the matrix entries. Since p preserves finite products, the matrix f determines x in p(T), including when either finite index set is empty.

Let R[T] be the free sheaf module on T. For each matrix coordinate define the map on R[T] that sends a generator [t] to that coordinate of t times [t]. The resulting finite matrix between coproducts of R[T] defines a module sheaf F as its cokernel. The normalized inverse-image-free-module comparison identifies its stalk generators with p(T).

Include the free modules at the generator x and project onto the coefficient of x. Both maps commute with the presentation matrices because each coordinate operator is diagonal in these generators. Their composite is identity, giving a retract of arrows. Apply the cokernel functor and use preservation of cokernels by module inverse image to obtain a retract of M in S(F). The normalized free comparison is chosen by a unique universal property, not from arbitrary unproved existence.
